conventions.fixture_paths: Paths are relative to the fixtures directory.
conventions.omitted_expected_fields: Fields absent from expected are not asserted.
conventions.null_values: A present null is an asserted null. This includes adherence_score when a conversation cannot be scored.
conventions.status_values: A status string is exact. An array of statuses means any one listed status satisfies the case.
conventions.evidence_indexes: Transcript evidence indexes are zero-based when a case includes them.
conventions.outcomes: outcome is evaluated, accepted, input_error, or unsupported.
conventions.basis: requirement means the graph or the input contract fixes the outcome. interpretation means the outcome follows the chosen conservative rubric. mixed means firm_fields and interpretation_fields name the expected keys, or node_statuses.<id>, that belong to each side.
conventions.criterion_ids_role: criterion_ids are the assertion vocabulary for this workflow. Evaluation criteria are still derived from node descriptions. 3.contact_number is a conditional subrequirement of 3.patient_information for new patients, not a sixth always-on scheduling criterion.
conventions.score: adherence_score is present only for the original conversation and for an empty transcript. The original conversation score is the mean of applicable per-criterion ratios times the valid-transition ratio, scaled and rounded to two decimals.

criterion_ids.description: Identify the assistant or its role
Invite the caller to state their need
Establish a provider preference or no preference
Establish whether the patient is new or returning
Establish the urgency of the issue
Obtain the patient details required for the established patient status
Obtain a contact number when the patient is new
Obtain caller acceptance of the offered appointment
Respond appropriately to the qualifying exception that occurred
Offer reminders or honor a stated refusal
Offer a chance to ask for further help

cases.title: Original conversation
cases.notes: Node 2 meets appointment type, provider preference, and returning-patient status. Urgency stays unresolved under the conservative reading. The earlier explanation of scheduling is not scheduling. The score is the mean of applicable per-criterion ratios times the valid-transition ratio, scaled and rounded to two decimals.

cases.title: Normal new patient
cases.notes: A new patient supplies full name, date of birth, and contact number before scheduling is complete. Contact number is the conditional subrequirement 3.contact_number of 3.patient_information.

cases.title: No error condition
cases.notes: When no qualifying exception occurs, node 4 is not applicable. That status is not a skipped step.

cases.title: Alternatives declined
cases.notes: The closing is assessed against the actual outcome, with no booked appointment after every alternative is declined.

cases.title: Returning patient without phone number
cases.notes: A returning patient does not need a contact number. Omitting 3.contact_number is not a penalty and does not leave 3.patient_information unmet.

cases.title: Patient volunteers required details
cases.notes: Count details the caller volunteers, including name, date of birth, patient status, and contact number when those details are required. A repeated question is not required.

cases.title: Patient cannot provide date of birth
cases.notes: The requirement is that node 3 is not incorrect: the caller cannot provide the date of birth. The reading is partial for node 3, not_reached for later nodes, and an incomplete verdict.

cases.title: First appointment rejected, second accepted
cases.notes: The first offer is declined and the second is accepted inside the same node 3 visit. That continuation is not a cycle.

cases.title: Semantically equivalent phrasing
cases.notes: A paraphrase such as birthday for date of birth satisfies the applicable request.

cases.title: Explaining a procedure
cases.notes: Describing the usual scheduling steps does not complete nodes 2 or 3. The reading treats both as not_reached because the call ends before scheduling begins.

cases.title: Promising future action
cases.notes: A promise to book is not confirmation. Node 3 is not completed on a promise alone.

cases.title: Requirement fulfilled across turns
cases.notes: Name and date of birth may be established on different turns and still satisfy 3.patient_information together.

cases.title: Multiple node actions in one turn
cases.notes: One assistant turn may support node 3 confirmation and node 5 closing at the same time.

cases.title: Interrupted or overlapping speech
cases.notes: Preserve the supplied turn order and intervals. Overlapping speech is not a workflow penalty and does not create an extra transition.

cases.title: Unrelated conversational detour
cases.notes: A complaint about a past visit is not a graph transition and is not node 4.

cases.title: Repeated question
cases.notes: A repeated question stays inside the same node visit. It does not add a path entry or a second credit for the same criterion.

cases.title: Corrected appointment offer
cases.notes: Judge the corrected time the caller accepts. An earlier offer that was replaced does not make the confirmation incorrect.

cases.title: Ambiguous urgency
cases.notes: A phrase such as nothing complicated does not by itself establish urgency.

cases.title: Caller declines reminders
cases.notes: If the caller already refused reminders, honoring that refusal satisfies 5.reminders. A second offer is not required.

cases.title: Corrected patient details
cases.notes: Use the date of birth the caller settles on after a correction. The replaced value does not remain the established one.

cases.title: Historical quoted action
cases.notes: A caller quoting a past assistant does not attribute that action to the current assistant. The quotation alone does not complete the quoted step.

cases.title: Ambiguous appointment acceptance
cases.notes: Maybe Tuesday is not acceptance. Consent is not inferred, so node 3 is not completed on that reply alone.

cases.title: Premature confirmation
cases.notes: Required actions are ordered. Confirmation before the necessary details or acceptance does not complete node 3. The reading allows incorrect or partial.

cases.title: Wrong provider confirmed
cases.notes: The confirmed provider differs from the provider the caller requested.

cases.title: Incorrect final appointment summary
cases.notes: The final summary names a different time than the one the caller accepted.

cases.title: Actual transition from node 2 to node 4
cases.notes: The graph has no transition from node 2 to node 4. A real move from node 2 into node 4 is an invalid transition.

cases.title: Early conversational clarification
cases.notes: Clarifying unclear speech before scheduling starts is incidental repair. It does not create a node 4 visit.

cases.title: Recovery followed by continued scheduling
cases.notes: After the unavailable slot is handled, later scheduling offers stay inside the same node 3 execution. The graph has no transition from node 4 back to node 3.

cases.title: Separate second booking attempt
cases.notes: A second distinct booking is not a legal transition on this graph. A new workflow instance does not add edges.

cases.title: Caller hangs up early
cases.notes: The caller ends the call before scheduling details. Later nodes are not skipped. The reading is not_reached.

cases.title: Assistant ends before required work
cases.notes: The assistant closes while the caller is ready to continue. The omitted applicable scheduling step is skipped.

cases.title: Confirmation without acceptance
cases.notes: Claiming the appointment is confirmed without caller acceptance is incorrect.

cases.title: User changes intent to cancellation
cases.notes: Cancellation is outside this graph. The call is not treated as a successful booking path.

cases.title: Claimed backend booking
cases.notes: A statement that the booking was saved may support conversational confirmation. It does not establish that a backend stored the appointment. No persistence result is expected.

cases.title: Missing required fields
cases.notes: A node missing data.description, or a turn missing a required field, is an input error.

cases.title: Unsupported transcript role
cases.notes: A role such as system is rejected. The supported roles are user and assistant.

cases.title: Invalid timestamps
cases.notes: A turn whose end is earlier than its beginning, or a non-numeric time, is an input error.

cases.title: Unsorted transcript starts
cases.notes: Turns whose start times decrease are an input error. The turns stay in the supplied order.

cases.title: Dangling graph edge
cases.notes: An edge whose target is not a node id, such as 9, is an input error.

cases.title: Cyclic or multi-start graph
cases.notes: A cycle is unsupported. A second start node is the same unsupported class.
